seoDescription: Explore the fundamentals of data handling in LlamaIndex by learning how to load data and create customized document objects from scratch. This video dives into the core concepts of Documents and Nodes, explaining their differences and relationships. You'll discover how to enrich your data with custom metadata, control its visibility to LLMs and embeddings, and format its string representation. Learn to build a custom data loader for Markdown files, a key step in building a sophisticated RAG chatbot.

chapters.title: Introduction: Loading Data and Documents
chapters.description: Introduces the video's focus on loading data and creating customized Document objects within the LlamaIndex framework.

chapters.title: Core Concepts: Documents vs. Nodes
chapters.description: Explains the fundamental distinction between Documents (entire files) and Nodes (chunks), and their key attributes like metadata and relationships.

chapters.title: Basic Document Creation and Loading
chapters.description: Demonstrates how to create a Document object from simple text and how to load multiple files from a directory.

chapters.title: Advanced Metadata Customization
chapters.description: Covers advanced techniques for customizing Documents, such as adding metadata, controlling its visibility, and formatting its text representation.

chapters.title: Building a Custom Markdown Document Loader
chapters.description: Explains the process and benefits of creating a custom data loader for Markdown files to gain full control over data ingestion.

chapters.title: Applying the Custom Loader in Practice
chapters.description: Demonstrates the practical application of the custom loader to ingest the LlamaIndex documentation into structured, categorized Document lists.

chapters.title: Inspecting and Customizing Loaded Documents
chapters.description: Shows how to inspect the metadata of loaded documents and apply custom templates to control their string formatting.

chapters.title: Controlling Metadata Visibility for LLMs and Embeddings
chapters.description: Illustrates how to selectively exclude metadata fields from being visible to the LLM and embedding models for finer-grained control.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Recap
chapters.description: Summarizes the key concepts covered in the video and points to resources for the custom Markdown loader code.

summary:
## Core Concepts: Documents & Nodes

*   **Document**: Represents an entire data source, such as a whole PDF, Word file, or Markdown file.
*   **Node**: A smaller chunk of an original `Document`. When you add `Document` objects to an index, they are automatically broken down into `Node` objects for efficient retrieval and processing.
*   **Attributes**: Both `Document` and `Node` objects can have two key attributes:
    *   **Metadata**: A dictionary of key-value pairs (e.g., `file_name`, `category`) that provides extra context.
    *   **Relationships**: Links between objects. For example, a `Node` automatically contains a reference to its parent `Document` ID.

## Basic Data Loading

You can create `Document` objects in two primary ways:

1.  **Manually**: Instantiate a `Document` object and pass text directly to it.
    ```python
    from llama_index.core.schema import Document
    doc = Document(text="This is the document content.")
    ```
2.  **Using Data Loaders**: Use a loader like `SimpleDirectoryReader` to ingest all files from a directory and convert them into a list of `Document` objects.
    ```python
    from llama_index.core import SimpleDirectoryReader
    documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./data").load_data()
    ```

## Advanced Document Customization

LlamaIndex offers granular control over how documents and their metadata are represented and used.

### Metadata Management

> [!NOTE]
> You can selectively control which metadata is visible to different parts of the RAG pipeline, like the LLM or the embedding model.

*   **Add Metadata**: Pass a dictionary to the `metadata` argument when creating a `Document`.
*   **Control Visibility**: Use the `excluded_llm_metadata_keys` and `excluded_embed_metadata_keys` attributes to hide specific metadata fields from the LLM and embedding model, respectively.

### Text Representation Customization

> [!TIP]
> Customizing text templates is a powerful way to structure the context that gets sent to the LLM, potentially improving response quality.

You can change how a `Document` object is converted into a string by setting these attributes:

*   `metadata_template`: A format string for each key-value pair in the metadata (e.g., `"{key}: {value}"`).
*   `metadata_seperator`: The string used to join the formatted metadata pairs (e.g., `", "`).
*   `text_template`: A template that defines the final layout of the metadata and the document content.

```python
# Example of setting a custom text template
doc.text_template = "Metadata:\n---\n{metadata_str}\n---\nContent:\n{content}"
```

## Building Custom Loaders

> [!IMPORTANT]
> While LlamaIndex provides many built-in loaders, creating your own gives you complete control over data parsing and document creation, which is invaluable for complex or unique data sources.

Building a custom loader is useful for:
*   Gaining a deeper understanding of the document creation process.
*   Implementing custom parsing logic tailored to your specific data structure.
*   For example, the custom Markdown loader in this video was built to associate code blocks with the text paragraphs that introduce them, creating a richer context for each node.
transcription:
## Introduction: Loading Data and Documents

Hey everyone, Logan here from LlamaIndex, back with another video on our series of Bottoms-Up development with LlamaIndex. We're on a quest to build a chatbot using the LlamaIndex documentation, but in a sort of like bottoms-up, low-level way. 

And so last episode we covered how to use LLMs in LlamaIndex, and in this video, we're going to cover how to load data and create document objects completely customized in LlamaIndex.

## Core Concepts: Documents vs. Nodes

So in LlamaIndex, there are documents and nodes. They're essentially the same, but the main difference is that a document is intended to represent the entire document, whether that's an entire page in a PDF, the entire PDF, entire Word file, etc.

And when you insert these documents into an index, they are broken down into nodes, which are basically smaller chunks of that original document used for retrieval and question answering and whatnot. And so these documents and nodes can have a few different attributes such as metadata, which can be something like a category or a file name, as well as relationships, which can be links to other nodes or documents. So for example, when you put a document inserted into an index, the nodes contain a reference to the parent document ID, and so that's an example of a relationship.

## Basic Document Creation and Loading

And we would see the actual usage for creating a document is super simple. We can import it, create it, give it some text, super easy. We can also import a `SimpleDirectoryReader` and read a directory of data and get a list of documents. So if we want to, you know, load all the data from our documentation to create a chatbot, we would just use the `SimpleDirectoryReader` and could load everything in our docs.

## Advanced Metadata Customization

We can also customize the documents quite heavily actually. Some advanced usage here, like I mentioned before, we can add metadata, so giving it in this case a category. We can also tell LlamaIndex to only use certain metadata for certain parts of LlamaIndex. So we can say, you know, we only want the embeddings to look at this metadata, or we only want the LLM to look at these metadata. And we can see here that we're saying we don't want the LLM to read the category metadata. So when this document or its nodes get sent to the LLM, the LLM doesn't know the category.

And on top of that, we can customize the representation of the metadata when this document gets transformed into a string. So we can set the separator between each metadata field in the dictionary. We could see what each key-value is formatted as. Here I've customized it with a little arrow. And then on top of that, when the metadata gets inserted next to the text, we can add a template for what that looks like. And here I've added a little label for metadata, a little line divider, a little label for the content. Super simple, but this allows for some pretty, I would say, complex representations and customization in LlamaIndex.

## Building a Custom Markdown Document Loader

So that's how to create documents. And now we're actually going to cover how we can, you know, create documents for the LlamaIndex documentation.

So I have a notebook here to cover that. What I've done ahead of time here is I've created a custom document loader for the markdown docs in LlamaIndex. So we're only going to worry about the markdown documents because we just want to keep the scope a little narrow, and we should still be able to get a useful chatbot with just our markdown documents in our documentation. And I've just made a function here to basically go through and parse the markdown, which is like a super structured format. We know where the headers are, we know where the code blocks are, and there's just a bunch of handling for that in here.

Now, while LlamaIndex does have a built-in markdown reader, building this on your own gets you one, more familiar with how to create documents, and two, if we ever need to customize further how these documents are being loaded, now we have straight access to how that's being loaded. For instance, here, one kind of customization that I did make was all the code blocks keep track of the paragraph above it, because often that paragraph above it is introducing that code block. So it's kind of like an extra piece of reference text that we can use later on, maybe we'll see, to help the question-answer process work better.

## Applying the Custom Loader in Practice

So just a quick demo of how this actually works. I'm going to append to my path here so I can actually load from my little folder here with my script. I made a quick helper function here to load the markdown documents, and here I'm just saying exclude everything except for markdown documents. We only want to, we only care about those. And then here I set a custom loader for that I was just showing. So basically what this does is it sets it up for .md files, we'll use my loader. And then lastly, I set recursive equal to True. Our documentation is a little nested, so it's going to recursively go through every folder and file and find every markdown file.

That's as simple as that. In I have a folder of all the documentation, every folder from our documentation. I'm loading it into separate lists of documents because each folder kind of captures a very specific part of LlamaIndex. So if you're building, you know, a chatbot over the documentation, it can be helpful to sort this ahead of time to make question answering easier later.

## Inspecting and Customizing Loaded Documents

So load those documents, it's pretty quick. And now we can just kind of investigate a little bit what this actually looks like. So I'm going to grab the agent docs there. You could see, you know, it's printed out all our metadata at the top here. So you can see we're keeping track of file name, content type is going to be either text or code, and the header path, which is like how nested the markdown headers are. So obviously right now we're at the top level, it's just 'module_guides'. If I go to maybe five here, now you can see the header path is 'data_agents/concept/tool_abstractions'. So this is just a way to help the LLM understand what documentation it's even looking at right now.

And again, you can access the metadata directly just by, you know, including that little `.metadata` attribute, and we can see here that it's formatted as a dictionary.

And that looks good, but we can actually customize this even further. We can set up our own text template. So like before we saw on the slides, we could add a little header for the metadata, a little separator, and then the content. We can customize the metadata template and then we can separate them by spaces. So now basically the metadata will be comma-separated list rather than line by line. So we can go through and apply this to all the docs in the agent docs list, and then we can go through and print the content from that doc. You'll notice here I've added a metadata mode, and this is what LlamaIndex uses under the hood to get the text for different parts of LlamaIndex. So there's a metadata mode for embeddings and for LLMs and then also all. And so you can see here that it fetches all the metadata in a single comma-separated line, and then we have our content following our template that we specified up here.

## Controlling Metadata Visibility for LLMs and Embeddings

Now we can get a bit more advanced with this customization. We could say that for the LLM metadata, so the metadata that the LLM reads, we don't want it to see the file name. So now when we call `get_content` with the metadata mode LLM, after applying this exclusion, we can see that the file name is no longer present in the text, which is what we wanted. And we can apply the same thing to the embeddings, and we see that also the embeddings no longer see the file name.

And so that's basically it.

## Conclusion and Recap

In this video we've covered how to create documents, the different ways you can customize them, and I'll provide links down below so you can read my markdown reader. It's not perfect, but it works and it's kind of an example of how you can build your own loaders. They're not scary, it just takes a little bit of time to write and then you have full control over how your data is loaded and what your documents look like. Hope this video was helpful and see you in the next.
